notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is day to day and has missed the last 17 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Michael Carcone is on injured reserve (upper-body surgery) and has missed the last 2 games.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-six forward.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 24 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in tied for sixth in the Central with 29 points, 2 points behind the Predators, tied for third. A regulation win for the Mammoth would pull them level with the Predators. The Predators have two games in hand.

NSH.head: Close, but the Mammoth have the slight edge
NSH.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators’ best way to tip it is a power play that gets going.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a slight edge
UTA.body: Even though Nashville has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Predators can still swing it if their power play gets going.

story.head: Kerfoot meets his old team
paras: The Predators have won two in a row, and the Mammoth (13-10-3) beat Minnesota 4-3 on Wednesday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Mammoth seventh (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Preds fourth (tied for tenth). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.558) says: their chances are worth about .695, and their goaltending has held them back. The Predators’ record (.646) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.542), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). As for the Predators, they keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest) and get their shots from in close (4th). They also get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st), so the Mammoth’s forecheck could keep them pinned in their own end. The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 24 A / 29 P in 25 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with seven goals in eleven games against Nashville since 2023-24. Logan Cooley (13 G / 15 A / 28 P in 23 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, with seven points in his last five games. For the Predators, Filip Forsberg (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Steven Stamkos (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 24 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Sebastian Cossa (6-3-1 / .881 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to go for Utah. Justus Annunen (4-2-0 / .863 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Nashville, but is expected to start.

At home, Andrew Brunette likes to send Schaefer, Kerfoot and Marchessault out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against O'Brien, Stenlund and But. Elsewhere, the Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.

The Mammoth are newly without Michael Carcone, and have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino and Nick Schmaltz for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
